newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indocement says to defend key markets.
newsitem.headline: Indocement says to defend key markets.

text.p: Indonesian cement maker PT Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa pledged on Tuesday to strongly defend its dominant market share position in the key Jakarta and West Java regions amid talk of rising competition.
"The firm is confident of its ability to defend its dominant market share position in Jakarta and West Java in the coming years," Indocement said in a statement following a shareholders meeting.
"Demand growth in the two key regions would be able to absorb additional supplies from new plants and it is expected that Java island would not experience significant oversupply," it said.
Java is the most densely inhabited island in Indonesia, with about 60 percent of the country's population of some 200 million.
Indocement president director Sudwikatmono told reporters after the meeting that he was confident that supply would remain low until the year 2000.
"Overupply could happen should all the 34 licence holders (to build new cement plants) realise their plans. Otherwise (supply) would continue to be low until the year 2000," he said.
Sudwikatmono said he was confident cement prices would remain steady and that small increases in cement prices were possible this year. He declined to give further details.
Indocement's market share in the two key regions, which represent 43 percent of total Indonesian demand, was 71 percent in 1996, Indocement said in a report.
Indocement's share of the total cement market across Indonesia was 38 percent in 1996, the report said.

Analysts said competitor Semen Cibinong in particular, which was expected to boost annual production capacity from 4.5 million tonnes in 1996 to 9.7 million tonnes in 1998, could encroach on Indocement's market share in the two key regions.

Indocement said its new plant in Cirebon, West Java together with two plants currently under way were expected to raise its current annual production capacity by 65 percent to 15.9 million tonnes before the end of 1999.
Indocement said its shareholders approved on Tuesday a move to pay a 70 rupiah dividend for 1996 against a total dividend of 160 rupiah for 1995.
